# Phi-3 Technical Report — A Highly Capable Language Model Locally on Your Phone

**Authors**: Marah Abdin and ~50 co-authors (Microsoft Research, corresponding)
**Year**: 2024
**Venue**: arXiv preprint cs.CL / cs.AI, 30 Aug 2024
**eprint / DOI**: arXiv:2404.14219
**Cited by**: [[primitives/INDEX]] entry [[PRIM-29]] (Recruitment-Adaptive Planning — local-model roster pool)

## Summary

[[Abdin-2024-Phi-3]] is the Microsoft technical report for the Phi-3 family of small language models (phi-3-mini 3.8B, phi-3-small 7B, phi-3-medium 14B, and the later phi-3.5 and phi-4 follow-ons referenced but not benchmarked here). The central claim is that a small model trained on a curated high-quality corpus ("textbook-quality" data) can match the benchmark performance of models 10× its size, including Mixtral 8×7B and GPT-3.5. The report documents the training pipeline (data curation, supervised fine-tuning, DPO), the tokenizer (extended vocab over tiktoken), the 4K / 128K context variants, and the iPhone-class device benchmarks that demonstrate on-device inference. The paper is the empirical evidence that local-SLM recruitment is a viable default for production agents, not just a research curiosity.

## Relevance to MAgHARCM

Phi-3 is the exemplar model for the [[PRIM-29]] recruitment pool. MAgHARCM's `internal/agents/recruit.go` chooses per-iteration agent configurations from a roster of local SLMs; Phi-3-mini and Phi-3.5-mini are the canonical "small specialist" entries alongside Qwen2.5-Coder, DeepSeek-Coder, StarCoder2, Yi-Coder, and Code Llama. The Phi-3 report's central result — that a 3.8B model can serve as a competent coding agent on a phone — underwrites MAgHARCM's design assumption that the [[PRIM-23]] chunked translator, [[PRIM-7]] verdict agents, and [[PRIM-25]] role-flip reviewer can all be Phi-3-mini-class models running locally under Ollama. The 128K context variant is also relevant to the [[PRIM-26]] Navigator's ≤ 4 KB tight-window discipline: knowing that even a small model can read 128K is the upper bound that justifies MAgHARCM's claim that the navigator never needs to spill into a second window.

## Hop-1 References

- [[Mixtral-2024]] — the open MoE baseline that Phi-3-mini matches at 1/10 the active-parameter budget; Mixtral is in the same MAgHARCM model roster pool.
- [[DeepSeek-Coder-2024]] — open code model family used in the same local-recruitment pool; complementary strengths (Phi-3 stronger on natural language, DeepSeek-Coder stronger on syntax).
- [[Code-Llama-2023]] — Meta's open code model; one of the older entrants that Phi-3 partially obsoletes for small-budget recruitment.
- [[StarCoder2-2024]] — large open code corpus; the kind of base model Phi-3-style curricula were tested against.

## Hop-2 Anchors (software-archaeology lean)

- [[Rajlich-1997]] — concept-locator analysis provides the offline "what is this model looking at" view that complements Phi-3's on-device transparency story.
- [[Foltz-2023]] — DR.JONES cognitive model predicts that small models will dominate on linear-traversal comprehension tasks; Phi-3's benchmarks confirm this empirically for code reading.
- [[Muller-2022]] — legacy modernization case studies show that the bottleneck is rarely model capacity and almost always data quality; Phi-3's textbook-quality-curriculum thesis is the modern SLM analogue.
